words.meaning: First aorist active infinitive of apostellw. Same verb as apestalken, above. Related to the word for apostles who set us free.
words.plain: Set at liberty [Greek: aposteilai — from the same root as 'apostle']. The word means to send out, release, dispatch. Isaiah's prophecy describes someone sent to release captives. Jesus reads this aloud and then announces it is fulfilled today — declaring himself the one sent to set people free.

words.meaning: Perfect passive participle of trauw, an old verb, but here only in the N.T. It means to break in pieces broken in heart and often in body as well.
words.plain: Them that are bruised [Greek: tetrausmenous] means broken — not just injured but shattered, in pieces. The word describes people crushed in body, in spirit, in dignity. Jesus is sent specifically to them. This is the core of his mission statement: he doesn't come for the already-fine.
